lines.watchItem: NVIDIA's data-centre sales reached $89.0 billion in its July quarter, up 117% from a year earlier, and it guided the next quarter to $108.0 billion. It guided the following fiscal year to about 70% growth while calling that figure supply-limited, so leading-edge wafer demand is running ahead of what the chain can build.

One buyer has reserved roughly 800,000 to 850,000 wafers of 2026 advanced-packaging capacity, over half the year's total, and packaging is pre-booked above 85% for 2026 and 2027 with the top three customers holding more than 85% of it. Reports still disagree on the size of the shortfall, one putting it at about 10% in mid-2026 and another at about 20% for the year.

NVIDIA says it has supply for about 70% of demand, its stacked-memory suppliers can meet only 60% to 70% of the volume requested for its next top-end part, and Micron says it can supply no more than about half of what customers ask for. Memory, not packaging alone, now sets how many accelerators actually ship.

NVIDIA is raising AI server system prices by more than 15% for shipments from early next year, while guiding its own gross margin to 74% with a stated floor of 71% to 72% because of memory costs. Samsung raised contract chipmaking prices 10% to 15% on new orders, so price increases are moving through several layers of the chain at once.

Microsoft is reported to be negotiating TSMC capacity for upward of 300,000 of its own Maia 300 chips for 2027 delivery, OpenAI's first custom inference chip is built on TSMC 3nm with Broadcom as design partner, and Anthropic is in early talks with Samsung about a custom chip on a 2nm process. The leading-node customer list is widening from merchant GPU vendors toward the model builders themselves.

Google has committed to more than 3 million units of Intel's bridge-style advanced packaging for its next in-house accelerator with 2028 delivery, Intel reports yield on that route above 90% and targets 2027 production at roughly half the cost of TSMC's CoWoS packaging, and TSMC announced a bridge-style packaging development with Kinsus in late July 2026. Intel holds about 13.7% of stacked-chip packaging capacity against TSMC's roughly 70%, and Intel's sole silicon-capacitor supplier for that route is already fully booked.

Washington is reported to be preparing tariffs on imported chips that would extend to finished data-centre servers, with duty-free import allowances sized to each company's US chip-fabrication investment; no rate or start date is given and the account says the plan could still change substantially. TSMC has announced an incremental $100 billion US investment linked to the January 2026 US-Taiwan trade and investment deal.

NVIDIA cut its financial guarantee for the OpenAI data-centre campus in Ohio from $250 billion to less than $120 billion, and reporting says it paused certain deals under a compute-partnership financing programme carrying $36 billion of commitments, which NVIDIA denies is halted. Part of the order flow behind leading-node volume rests on the chip vendor's own credit support rather than on customer cash.
